spec_match.rationale: The rule uses the real correlated-jitter idiom the spec's caching section exists for — one --lean cache slot shared between rotate and a calc()-multiplied translate — and the JS fallback reproduces the same correlation.

interactive.rationale: Tilt, offset and card-count sliders, Reshuffle and Turn-it-all-off all rebuild the pinboard, and the readout reports distinct angles and spread measured from computed style.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises restrained jitter plus the old inline-style way for comparison, and both columns are present with per-approach cost lines.

edge_cases.rationale: Zero-everything is a narrated explicit state, the taste threshold (>8°) is called out, and the unsupported browser gets the labelled JS path that the right-hand column documents.

conformance.rationale: The dashed-ident cache-slot assertion in the feature suite covers exactly the --lean sharing this page depends on.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: 9 cards with 9 distinct computed rotate angles spanning 17.1° at tilt 12, the >8° taste warning appeared, Turn-it-all-off reset computed rotate to 0deg with the plain-grid narration; banner honestly reports the JS path on this browser; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Builds log and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('board-built', …) with tilt, offset, count, distinct angles and support flag.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, secondary button overrides background and color, 44px controls, prefers-reduced-motion guard present.

accessibility.rationale: Controls are labelled and the readout is aria-live, but the pinboard cards are plain divs with headings — fine — while the decorative tilt state itself is only conveyed by the measured-angles sentence; acceptable, though the board carries no group label tying it to the readout.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; the board's auto-fill columns collapse cleanly on mobile in the screenshot.

openQuestions.title: Same supported-path re-roll assumption as scatter-field
openQuestions.detail: Reshuffle relies on sheet.replaceSync() with unchanged rule text producing new random() values on a supporting browser; per CSS Values 5 the values are specified to be stable, so on Chrome 155 Reshuffle may only change anything because the cards are recreated (new elements do get fresh per-element values — which likely saves this page, unlike scatter-field's adopted-sheet assumption; both need one verification pass on Chrome 155/Canary). Not verifiable on Chromium 141, where random() is unsupported.

summary: A genuinely tasteful practical demo: correlated jitter through a shared --lean cache slot, an honest labelled JS path on non-supporting browsers, and measured (not asserted) angle distinctness. Verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/css-random-function/organic-ui/ — tilt to 12° produced 9 distinct angles spanning 17.1° with the restraint warning, the off state computed to rotate:0deg, console clean, no overflow on either device class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 0 pass / 8 fail, all honest pre-155 gaps.
